male.text: I feel like watching a movie tonight.

female.text: I feel like watching a movie tonight.

male.text: I'd like a copy of the schedule.

female.text: I'd like a copy of the schedule.

male.text: How much does a round-trip ticket cost?

female.text: How much does a round-trip ticket cost?

male.text: Bring useful items such as a flashlight and a map.

female.text: Bring useful items such as a flashlight and a map.

male.text: I prefer fresh fruit to candy.

female.text: I prefer fresh fruit to candy.

male.text: I usually take the stairs instead of the elevator.

female.text: I usually take the stairs instead of the elevator.

male.text: Did you see the movie yesterday?

female.text: Did you see the movie yesterday?

male.text: By the time we arrived, the movie had started.

female.text: By the time we arrived, the movie had started.

male.text: Could you tell me whether the elevator is working?

female.text: Could you tell me whether the elevator is working?

male.text: Is there an elevator in this building?

female.text: Is there an elevator in this building?

male.text: I never throw trash in the street.

female.text: I never throw trash in the street.

male.text: I met my neighbor in the elevator.

female.text: I met my neighbor in the elevator.

male.text: I eat fruit instead of candy after lunch.

female.text: I eat fruit instead of candy after lunch.

male.text: When is the school break this year?

female.text: When is the school break this year?

family-weekend.title: A family visit on the weekend.
signature: Would you like to visit our grandparents this weekend?
I used to visit them every Friday. I want to see them again.
Let's take some fruit with us.
It's worth leaving early so we can spend more time with them.
Shall we take lunch with us?
Let's bring some fruit instead; they've already planned lunch.

tailor-pickup.title: Picking up a garment.
signature: When is the earliest I can pick up the pants?
I can finish the hem tomorrow afternoon.
As soon as they're ready, I'll come by.
I'll text you before five. Let me know if you need to come the following morning instead.
Thanks, can I try it on before I leave?
Yes, there's a fitting room in the back.

seat-on-train.title: A seat on the train.
signature: Are there any free seats in this train car?
There are two by the window.
Can I put my bag on the rack?
Sure. Do you mind if I take the window seat?
Not at all. I'll take the aisle seat.
Thanks, I like to look out the window on this route.

book-recommendation.title: Recommending a book.
signature: I'm interested in hiking. Do you know any books for beginners?
The book that I borrowed last week has some easy routes.
Does it tell you what to bring?
Yes. It lists useful items such as a flashlight and a map. It's worth reading before your first trip.
Is there a copy at the library?
I think so; I'll send you the title so you can check.

online-lesson-audio.title: Trouble hearing the online lesson.
signature: I can't hear you clearly. Could you please repeat the last sentence?
Let me check the microphone. Can you hear me now?
Yes. I didn't catch the first part because the sound cut out.
I'll start the sentence again and write it in the chat too.
Thanks, I can read the chat even when the sound cuts out.
I'll send the slides afterward too, so you can review the examples.

equipment-repair.title: Repairing equipment.
signature: Did you find out why the printer kept jamming?
Yes. I decided to check the back because the front tray was clear.
Was there any paper stuck back there?
A torn sheet was stuck inside, so I removed it with the power off. I managed to print a test page afterward.
Has anyone tried printing several pages in a row?
Not yet; let's run a small batch before we send the full job.

tea-with-a-guest.title: Offering tea to a guest.
signature: Would you like tea or coffee?
I'd like a cup of tea, please. I like it without sugar.
Here you are. It's hot, so be careful.
Thank you for making it. It smells lovely.
You're welcome. Please help yourself to a cookie.
Thanks, I'll just have one with the tea.

team-options.title: Choosing a project solution.
signature: I believe a short online form is the quickest way to collect feedback.
I don't agree with using an online form alone. Some visitors don't have internet access.
Printing separate forms would take more time. However, we could leave one tablet at reception.
Good idea. In addition to the tablet, let's keep a few paper copies for anyone who needs one.
Who will collect the paper forms afterward?
I'll collect them and enter the answers before we compare the results.

new-flat-tour.title: A tour of a new apartment.
signature: How is the new apartment? Is it big enough?
Yes. There is a small balcony, and there are two bedrooms.
These are your new keys, right?
Yes. The round one opens the main door.
And which one opens the storage room?
The small square one; keep it on the same ring for now.

choosing-a-course.title: Choosing an evening course.
signature: What do you look for in an evening class?
Do you mean the subject or the schedule?
Both. Why do you prefer the smaller class?
I get more time to speak. Which one would you choose?
I'd try the smaller class if there are still places.
I'll call to ask if I can attend one lesson before I sign up.

saturday-train-plans.title: Saturday train plans.
signature: Are you going to drive to the coast on Saturday?
No. I'm not going to drive there. The roads get busy.
I'm going to take the train too. Shall we book together?
Yes. I'm planning to return in the evening. Does that work for you?
Yes, as long as we catch the last bus home afterward.
I'll check when it leaves before I book the return train.

first-interview-introduction.title: Introducing yourself in an interview.
signature: Good morning. My name is Omar Ali. I'm here for the interview.
Welcome, Omar. What do you do at the moment?
I'm a sales associate. I have two years of experience with customers.
Thank you. Could you tell me about a busy day at your shop?
On Saturdays we usually answer questions while people line up to pay.
Would I start on the register or help people on the shop floor?

quieter-carriage.title: A quieter train car.
signature: Do you mind if I sit by the window?
Not at all. Would you mind moving your bag off the aisle seat?
Of course. I'm sorry for leaving it there.
That's all right. There's plenty of room above us.
Thanks, I'll move my bag up there so the seat is free.
Good idea; it usually gets busy at the next stop.

a-note-for-the-neighbour.title: A note for a neighbor.
signature: I feel like baking something for our new neighbors.
How about making muffins and leaving a note?
Good idea. I'll start with “My name is Omar.”
Yes. You could add that we're next door if they need anything.
Should we write our apartment number on the note?
Yes, add it beneath our names so they know which door to knock on.

introducing-a-new-teammate.title: Introducing a new teammate.
signature: Welcome to the team. My name is Omar, and this is the support desk.
Nice to meet you. Who is on the afternoon shift?
Lina. I'll introduce you when she gets here.
Thanks. I'd like to see how she handles new requests.
I'll ask her if you can sit in on the next call.
Thanks, I'll write down my questions and ask her afterward.

l2-005.title: Checking the window before leaving.
signature: Can we leave for the station now?
I forgot to close the window.
I'll wait by the elevator while you close it.
The handle won't turn all the way; can you give me a hand?
Lift the window slightly while you turn it.
That worked. Now we can leave without worrying about the rain.

l2-011.title: Looking forward to another visit.
signature: I had a lovely time today. Shall we meet next month?
I'm looking forward to seeing you again.
I'll send you a couple of dates once I get home.
Please include a weekday if you can; weekends are hard for me.
I'll see if Thursday works, and we could have lunch nearby.
That sounds good; I'd like to show you the new market afterward.

l2-015.title: Meeting on the coast.
signature: Is the coast close enough to walk from here?
It's about three kilometers from here to the coast.
That's fine. Let's leave enough time to get back before dark.
Could we eat near the harbor so we don't have to drive again?
Yes, I'll find a place within walking distance of the parking lot.
I'll bring a warm jacket in case it's windy by the water.

l2-019.title: Finding someone to help with math.
signature: Can you help me check these fractions?
Great. Could you show me one example before I try the rest?
Sure; let's start by writing the numbers in the same units.
So should I turn the meters into centimeters first?
Yes. After that, add them and check that your answer is reasonable.

l2-033.title: A new French practice agreement.
signature: We keep switching to English when the exercises get harder.
From now on, we'll only speak French.
Agreed. If I get stuck, I'll try to explain the word in French.
And if I don't understand, I'll ask you to say it another way.
Shall we write down the words we had trouble with afterward?
Yes, we'll use those words to start our next conversation.

l2-044.title: A short business trip.
signature: Where did you go for your meeting last week?
I went to Boston for five days on a business trip.
Did you have time to visit the city after the meetings?
Only for an hour. I walked around the old market near my hotel.
Would you stay in the same area next time?
Yes, I could walk to the meetings and still find somewhere to eat afterward.

l2-051.title: How long have you studied French.
signature: How many years have you been studying French?
I've been studying French for three years.
Then you'll be fine in the conversation group. We meet on Thursdays.
Do I need to understand everything people say?
At this time, you don't need to understand everything.
Then I'll focus on catching the main idea and ask about new words afterward.

l2-053.title: Looking for an apartment near work.
signature: I'm looking for an apartment to rent.
Do you want to live near work or near the station?
Near the station, as long as it's on a quiet street.
There's an apartment two streets back; do you want to see it after work?
Yes, and I'd like to hear how noisy it is at that time of day.
I'll ask to visit before sunset so we can check the light as well.

l2-061.title: Comparing two cities.
signature: Have you been to Boston or Chicago in the past three weeks?
Yes, I was in both cities last month.
In some ways, Boston is nicer than Chicago.
What did you like most about Boston?
I could walk to the shops and the library from my apartment.
That's something I miss too; here I usually need the bus.

l2-079.title: Whose turn is it to take out the trash.
signature: We have to put the bin outside before seven.
It's my turn to take out the trash.
Thanks. I'll bring the empty bin back in the morning.
Can you rinse it before you put it away?
Yes, I'll leave it in the sun until it's dry.
Thanks; there are spare bin bags under the sink.

l2-088.title: Getting used to a new neighborhood.
signature: How are you settling into the new apartment?
I'm starting to get used to living here.
Would you like me to show you the nearest shops this weekend?
Yes, I still haven't found a place that sells fresh bread.
There's a bakery behind the small market, but it closes at noon.
Let's go early on Saturday so I can pick up breakfast.

l2-098.title: Politely changing the subject.
signature: We've already talked about the schedule.
Would you mind if I change subjects?
Not at all. What would you like to talk about?
Could we talk about how the course went instead?
Sure. Which activity helped you speak the most?
The one where we had to solve a problem together without reading a script.

l2-106.title: Agreeing on a pickup time.
signature: When should I come pick you up tomorrow?
My flight lands at four, but I'll need time to get my bag.
I'll be outside at half past four. Text me if the flight is late.
Can we meet by the short-stay parking lot instead of the main doors?
Yes, call me when you've collected your bag and I'll drive over.
I'll send you the exit number once I see the sign.

l2-124.title: Asking where to put your coat.
signature: Come in. Everyone's in the living room.
Where should I put my coat?
On the hook by the door. There's a free one on the left.
Thanks. Is it all right if I leave my wet umbrella there too?
Put the umbrella in the stand so the floor stays dry.
Good idea. I'll shake off the extra water outside first.

l2-126.title: Talking about your Saturday morning.
signature: What time do you usually get up on Saturday?
At around eight. On weekdays I get up at six.
Let's have breakfast at nine, then.
Do we have time to stop at the market afterward?
Yes, if we go straight there before it gets busy.
I'll take a bag so we don't have to buy one there.

l2-129.title: Opening a meeting on a positive note.
signature: We have two updates today, one good and one difficult.
Let's start with the good news.
The new schedule was approved this morning.
That's good news. When will people start using it?
On Monday, but we need to share the changes before Friday.
I'll draft a short note highlighting the shifts that moved.

l2-141.title: Making a room bright enough to study.
signature: I'll move the lamp closer to the desk.
Thanks. Now I can see the small print.
Is the light shining directly on your screen now?
A little; could you turn the lamp toward the wall?
Like this? You can still move it closer to the book if you need to.

l2-152.title: Leaving earlier to avoid the rush.
signature: Should we leave at noon or wait until after lunch?
The sooner you leave, the better.
All right. I'll pack lunch so we can leave before noon.
Do you think we'll find parking if we arrive at one?
Probably, but there's a second parking lot behind the station if the first is full.
I'll save both locations so we don't have to look them up on the way.

l2-180.title: Inviting someone to choose an outfit.
signature: I've put the outfits for the family event in this room.
Thanks. I'll pick something I can also wear to work.
Try the plain jacket; it goes with both pairs of pants.
It fits well. Is the fabric light enough for summer?
Yes, and you can wear a warm layer underneath when it gets cooler.

l2-183.title: Planning around morning traffic.
signature: Can we drive across town at eight tomorrow?
There's a lot of traffic here in the mornings.
Then we'll take the train and walk from the station.
How long is the walk once we get off?
About twelve minutes if we use the west exit.
I'll check which train car stops closest to that exit.

l2-200.title: Keeping a decision open to discussion.
signature: Does the draft mean the new schedule has already been decided?
Good. I'd like to suggest a later start for the evening group.
What would be the advantage of starting later?
More people could come after work, but we'd have less time in the room.
Let's ask the group which time they can manage before we book it.

l3-008.title: Asking for an accessible restroom.
signature: Excuse me, can you help me?
Sure. Are you looking for something in the terminal?
Can you show me where the bathroom is?
There is an accessible one beside the elevators.
Can we get there without using the stairs?
Yes. Go straight ahead and turn right at the information desk.

l3-011.title: Welcoming a new neighbor for tea.
signature: I didn't expect to see you here.
I just moved into the apartment upstairs. My name is Sara.
I'm Omar. Please come in; I was about to put the kettle on.
Would you like a cup of tea?
Yes, please. I've heard the courtyard is open to everyone.
It is. We can take our tea outside if you'd like.

l3-015.title: Recognizing an old classmate.
signature: Do you remember the first time we met?
We were waiting outside the wrong classroom, weren't we?
I was a student at that time.
So was I. I used to carry a paper schedule everywhere.
Now I put everything on my phone and still mix up the rooms.
Some things never change. Shall we catch up over lunch?

l3-020.title: Discussing a movie without spoilers.
signature: I usually pick comedies, but there's a documentary I'd recommend.
Do you watch it in English or with subtitles?
With subtitles the first time. It was easier to follow.
Can you tell me a bit about it without giving away the ending?
It follows a group of volunteers restoring an old bridge.
I'd like to watch that. What's the title?
This is one of my favorite movies.

l3-049.title: Asking about a school program.
signature: Yes, I started here last term. Are you thinking of applying?
This is one of the best schools in the city.
That's what I heard too. Do you want to see the language department?
I'd like to find out whether they offer evening classes.
I'll introduce you to someone who can explain the schedule.

l3-078.title: Working out where the noise came from.
signature: Was it coming from the street or from inside the building?
It sounded like something had fallen in the hallway.
What did you hear when you opened the door?
All of a sudden, a dog began barking.
There is a dog in the apartment next door. It may have heard the same noise.

l3-093.title: Reconsidering how to prepare for a test.
signature: How did Tom feel about his results after the test?
In retrospect, Tom wishes he had spent more time studying.
I should have spread out my own practice too. I left it all until the night before.
You can plan differently for the next one.
Would you help me make a schedule for next week?
I certainly don't mind helping you.

l3-110.title: Making peace over a shared space.
signature: I'd like to talk about the boxes in the shared hallway.
The last thing I want to do is cause you any problems.
I understand. What matters is that everyone can get through safely.
I'll move them into my apartment this evening.
Thanks. I can help you lift the heavier ones.
Let's try to treat each other with respect.

l3-114.title: Asking whether a friend needs a ride.
signature: Would you like me to drive over and collect you?
Don't bother to pick me up at the hotel.
Are you going to take the shuttle to the station instead?
Yes, it stops outside the hotel every half hour.
That saves us a trip. Let me know when you're on board.

l3-162.title: Asking about a family member's appointment.
signature: He's back home. He said the next visit was on Thursday.
Do you know where the follow-up clinic is?
It's in the same building, on the first floor.
I can take him there if he needs a ride.
There's no need to worry about Tom.
Still, I'll ask whether he would like some company.

l3-171.title: Keeping in touch during a power cut.
signature: I can't imagine living without electricity.
I know. We use it for almost everything at home.
Is there a charged flashlight in the drawer?
Yes. I'll bring it over. Is your phone still working?
Yes, but the battery is getting low. I'll use it only for messages.
I'll walk back now. Please leave the flashlight by the door.

a1-nice-to-meet-you.title: Nice to meet you.
signature: Hi, I'm Omar. What's your name?
I'm Sara. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too, Sara.

a1-say-that-again.title: Could you say that again.
signature: Could you say that again, please?
Of course. Your order is ready.

a1-good-to-see-you.title: Good to see you.
signature: Hi, Sara. Good to see you.
Good to see you too! How's it going?
Pretty good, thanks. See you later!

a1-ask-for-the-check.title: Asking for the check.
signature: Can I get the check, please?
